note: 2022 MCM A, team 2216547. 21 figure rows (19 numbered plus the two uncaptioned leaflet items on p24/p25) and 3 printed tables, over 30 measured regions with 6 exclusions, unaccounted = 0. Shapes that need reading before the fields make sense: Figure 1 is two anatomical views inside one box; Figures 12, 13 and 14 are four-panel stacks with a legend above the stack and tick labels only under the bottom panel; Figures 15, 16, 17 and 19 are two- and three-panel stacks whose panels carry different variables, and 16 and 19 print their labels outside to the right; and Figure 18 is not a chart at all but six rider pictograms with printed percentages. Three exhibits are three-dimensional - Figure 8 (three isometric route views in one row), Figure 11 (three state planes along a distance axis) and the p25 route - and none of them shades a surface. Two tables (p5, p14) have a measured region that covers the header band only; their data rows run on as text without a region, which the rows declare. The last two pages are a two-column leaflet, not an appendix: p24 carries banner headlines, a masthead logo and an uncaptioned reprint of Figure 5's power curve, p25 carries the same logo and an uncaptioned 3-D route, and neither item is cited anywhere. Printing errors kept verbatim: Figure 2's caption promises handwriting that was typeset, Figure 4's caption says E0 while its legend names Rouleur_top/middle/low, Figure 15 drops the space in 'Distribution,the' and spells 'Time Trail', and the p20 velocity axis is fine but the p13 equation is set with the fraction bar detached. Five printed headings are missing from the extractor's index (4.4.2, 5.2.1, 5.2.2, 5.5 and the leaflet banners); the single-line ones are recorded verbatim from the text layer and 5.5, which wraps, is recorded as 未编号标题 with its number kept.
rules: The paper is built in three exhibit regimes and the section tells you which one you are in: the model sections 4.1-4.4 carry one schematic or one power curve per subsection and never two charted results, section 5 is the only place where four-panel result charts appear, and the two-page leaflet at the back repeats existing artwork without numbers or captions [place.section_kind] [geometry.family] [caption.numbering].

Depth appears three times and always as a coordinate frame rather than a surface: the route views in Figure 8, the state planes of Figure 11 and the leaflet route on p25 are all isometric boxes, and no exhibit in the paper draws a mesh floor, a colour ramp or shaded surfaces [geometry.three_d] [geometry.panel_count].

Panel count tracks the number of things being compared, and the legend follows the panels: one panel gets an inside box, four stacked panels get one legend block above the stack, and the two three-panel figures on p20/p21 print their labels outside to the right instead, because a legend box would have covered the curves [geometry.panel_count] [geometry.legend].

Table shape follows the data rather than the page: the notation glossary is tall and thin (18 rows by 3 columns) because it lists symbols, the parameter tables are wide and short because they hold one row per rider, and only the paper's single numbered table puts units in its header while the other two write them inside the cells [table.rows] [table.cols] [table.units_in_header].

Captions are noun phrases, never sentences: every numbered figure and table caption ends in a noun or a place name and no caption carries a verb, a unit or a conclusion, which is why the reading of every figure has to be reconstructed from the body sentence instead of the caption [caption.voice] [caption.words] [caption.concludes].

Three captions describe artwork that is not there: Figure 2 promises handwriting that is typeset, Figure 4 names E0 while the legend varies the rider, and Figure 15 both misses a space after a comma and spells 'Trail' without its second i - so a consumer keying on captions will mismatch the figure and the parameter [caption.verbatim] [geometry.family].

Exhibits are introduced by a numbered pointer in only a third of the cases; the rest are deictic ('as shown in the figure', 'as follows:') or reached through the caption alone, and the numbered pointers mostly sit inline in a running sentence rather than opening one [mention.lead_pattern] [mention.lead_pages].

Reading sentences follow the artwork, not precede it: nine rows carry a sentence after the figure that names the number and reads the curves back, and no row carries one before [mention.trail_sentence] [mention.read_sentences].

Two artwork items are reprinted outside the numbered sequence - the leaflet's power curve (identical to Figure 5) and its 3-D route - and both are recorded with caption_source = none and no mention, because the leaflet cites nothing and nothing cites it [caption_source] [mention.count].

tables.note: Unnumbered notation glossary under the heading '3 Notations': 18 symbol rows under a three-column head (Symbols / Description / Unit), booktabs with no vertical rules and no shading. The unit is its own column, so the header carries no unit; italic symbol cells sit in the left column and the right column mixes W, J, kg, m/s and bare 1. The measured region covers only the header band between the first two rules - the 18 data rows run on to y = 637.18 as text with no region of their own, and the sentence 'where we define the main parameters...' below the bottom rule is body prose rather than a table note.
